story.title: Early Voting Insights in South Carolina Senate Race Ahead of Trump Visit
story.summary: As early voting progresses in South Carolina, over 671,000 residents have cast their ballots, though current totals do not indicate a clear leader in the Senate race. The early voting data reflects a broader trend, with more than 42 million Americans participating in early voting nationwide, suggesting heightened enthusiasm ahead of the midterm elections.

explore_lenses.label: What does the early-vote surge actually show?
explore_lenses.title: Record turnout, not a candidate lead
explore_lenses.summary: South Carolina’s early-vote total is historically high for a gubernatorial-year general election, but turnout reports measure ballots cast rather than votes for Senate candidates. The available data therefore signals participation, not which candidate is ahead.

claims.text: The South Carolina Election Commission said that nearly 564,000 early ballots had been cast by 3 p.m. on October 26, exceeding the prior gubernatorial-election early-voting record of 561,563 set in 2022.

The Commission’s participation page distinguishes an early-voting turnout report from absentee statistics by race; its early-voting report is a turnout measure, not a published Senate preference tally.

Forecast: High early participation alone cannot reliably identify the Senate leader, because the Commission says early-voting results are reported on election night rather than during the early-voting period.

explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: The packet’s 671,000 figure is later than the Commission’s October 26 record announcement, but a public turnout total does not reveal the candidates selected.

explore_lenses.label: Why is Trump returning to South Carolina?
explore_lenses.title: A normally safe seat has become competitive
explore_lenses.summary: Trump’s visit is an effort to turn out Republican voters for appointed Sen. Darline Graham in a race that reporting describes as unexpectedly close. The candidates and their supporters are making contrasting appeals rather than arguing from early-vote totals.

claims.text: Darline Graham was appointed by Gov. Henry McMaster in July to fill the remainder of her late brother Lindsey Graham’s Senate term, then became the Republican nominee in August for a full six-year term.
Trump’s October 29 Rock Hill appearance was his second South Carolina visit that month; AP reported that Republicans viewed holding the seat as essential to retaining their Senate majority.

Graham has characterized Democrat Annie Andrews as too liberal and accused her of misrepresenting Graham’s record, while Andrews has asked voters to give a Democrat "a chance" and said they could remove her after six years if dissatisfied.
Forecast: A WFAE-reported review of public polling found Graham ahead by 1 to 3 points, generally within poll margins of error; that is a snapshot rather than a prediction of the result.

explore_lenses.label: When will early votes become Senate results?
explore_lenses.title: Early voting ends October 31; results begin November 3
explore_lenses.summary: Voters may cast early ballots through Saturday, October 31, before Election Day on Tuesday, November 3. The state plans to include early-voting results in its unofficial election-night reporting, with a mandatory recount threshold for very close contests.

claims.text: For the November 3 statewide general election, South Carolina early voting runs from October 19 through October 31, with centers open 8:30 a.m. to 6 p.m. Monday through Saturday.
The South Carolina Election Commission says early-voting results for all locations are reported on election night and included in unofficial results.
The Commission says a recount is mandatory if the margin between the winning candidate and any nonwinning candidate is 1% or less of the total votes cast for that office.

story_report.summary: More than 671,000 South Carolinians have voted early in the statewide election, part of a nationwide early-voting total exceeding 42 million. The turnout has not produced a public indication of who leads the Senate contest, because the state’s early-voting reporting is a turnout measure rather than a candidate-preference tally. The immediate consequence is that the race remains unresolved ahead of Election Day despite heavy campaigning and high participation.

sections.heading: Senate Race Draws Trump Attention
sections.body: Darline Graham was appointed in July to complete the Senate term of her late brother, Lindsey Graham, and then won the Republican nomination for a full six-year term in August. Trump’s Oct. 29 appearance in Rock Hill was his second South Carolina visit that month, as Republicans regarded retaining the seat as important to preserving their Senate majority. Graham has called Democrat Annie Andrews too liberal, while Andrews has urged voters to give a Democrat a chance; a review of public polling found Graham ahead by 1 to 3 points, generally within margins of error.

sections.heading: Early Voting Results Await Election Night
sections.body: For the Nov. 3 statewide general election, early voting runs from Oct. 19 through Oct. 31, with voting centers open from 8:30 a.m. to 6 p.m. Monday through Saturday. The South Carolina Election Commission says results from all early-voting locations will be reported on election night as part of the unofficial totals. A recount is mandatory when the margin between the winner and any nonwinning candidate is 1% or less of votes cast for the office.

unresolved.text: The public early-voting total does not show how ballots were marked, so it cannot establish which Senate candidate leads before election-night reporting.
Election-night results will be unofficial and may change through canvassing, a recount or challenges; the final timetable depends on the reported margin and any challenges.

related_stories.title: Investigation Launched into Alaska Senate Candidate Over Alleged Spoiler Scheme
related_stories.summary: Alaska Governor Mike Dunleavy has ordered an investigation into Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola's campaign. This follows allegations that her campaign recruited a second candidate named Dan Sullivan to confuse voters and dilute support for the incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan. Donald Trump has also called for Peltola's prosecution over these claims.

related_stories.title: Israel's Election Deadlock and Upcoming GDP Report Insights
related_stories.summary: As nearly 90% of votes from Israel's election have been counted, no clear winner has emerged, leading to expectations of difficult coalition negotiations. The pro-Netanyahu bloc holds a slight lead over the anti-Netanyahu bloc, but neither is projected to secure a majority. Meanwhile, economists anticipate that the upcoming GDP report will indicate economic growth, albeit described as 'fragile.'

related_stories.title: Putin Hosts African Leaders at Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow
related_stories.summary: President Vladimir Putin welcomed nearly two dozen African leaders to the Kremlin for a two-day Russia-Africa summit. This event is part of Russia's strategy to strengthen ties with African nations, aiming to enhance its influence on the continent, which has a population of approximately 1.6 billion people.
